questions.q: You're restoring a full backup followed by a differential backup as the final step. Which option goes on the full backup restore?
options: WITH NORECOVERY, so more backups can still be applied on top
No option is needed — the default already leaves it restoring
WITH RECOVERY, so the database comes online right away
WITH STANDBY, so the database is read-only
questions.explain: Every step except the last one in a restore sequence uses NORECOVERY, keeping the database in RESTORING state so later backups can still be applied.

questions.q: What happens once a database has been restored WITH RECOVERY?
options: The database is permanently placed in read-only mode
You can still restore additional log backups on top at any time
No further differential or log backups can be restored on top without starting the sequence over from the full backup
The transaction log is automatically truncated for the next 24 hours
questions.explain: RECOVERY rolls back uncommitted transactions and brings the database online, which ends the restore sequence.

questions.q: What does RESTORE FILELISTONLY actually do?
options: Lists every backup ever taken of a given database
Reads a backup file's header and lists its logical/physical file names, without restoring any data
Restores only the data files, skipping the log file
Verifies that every page in the backup is readable
questions.explain: FILELISTONLY reads just the header of a backup to reveal the LogicalName/PhysicalName pairs you need for the MOVE clause.

questions.q: Why would you use the MOVE clause on a RESTORE DATABASE statement?
options: To convert a full backup into a differential backup
To relocate a restored file to a different physical path than the one recorded in the backup
To rename the database itself
To move the backup file from one disk folder to another before restoring
questions.explain: Without MOVE, SQL Server tries to write restored files to the exact original paths — if those paths don't exist on the target, the restore fails.

questions.q: What state is a database in immediately after RESTORE DATABASE ... WITH NORECOVERY completes?
options: OFFLINE — taken permanently offline
SUSPECT — flagged as corrupted
ONLINE — fully usable immediately
RESTORING — not yet usable, waiting for more backups or an explicit recovery
questions.explain: NORECOVERY intentionally leaves the database in a RESTORING state so the rest of the backup chain can still be applied.
